questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No card is a parcel. All cards are envelopes. Some envelopes are bags. Conclusions: I. All envelopes can never be parcels. II. No card is a bag. III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
No card is a parcel.
All cards are envelopes.
Some envelopes are bags.

Conclusions:
I. All envelopes can never be parcels.
II. No card is a bag.
III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All envelopes can never be parcels → Follow (As no card is a parcel and all cards are envelopes. As whole card comes in envelopes and cannot be parcel, therefore it is true.)

II. No card is a bag → Does not follow (As no card is a parcel, all cards are envelopes and some envelopes are bags. As no direct relation is given between card and bags, therefore it is possible but not definite.)

III. At least some bags are postcards → Does not follow (As no relation with postcards is given, therefore it is false).

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tears are drops. Some drops are streams. All streams are rivers. Conclusions: I. All tears can never be rivers. II. Some drops are rivers. III. All tears being streams is a possibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
Some tears are drops.
Some drops are streams.
All streams are rivers.

Conclusions:
I. All tears can never be rivers.
II. Some drops are rivers.
III. All tears being streams is a possibility.

options.text: Both I and II conclusion follow
options.html: Both I and II conclusion follow

options.text: Both II and III conclusion follow
options.html: Both II and III conclusion follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All tears can never be rivers → Does not follow (As some tears are drops, some drops are streams and all streams are rivers. As no direct relation is given between tears and rivers, therefore it is false.)

II. Some drops are rivers → Follow (As some drops are streams and all streams are rivers. As whole streams comes in rivers and has some part common with drops, therefore it is true.)

III. All tears being streams is a possibility → Follow (As some tears are drops, some drops are streams. As no statements restricts tears from being streams, therefore it is possible.)

∴ Here, Both II and III conclusion follow.

questions.questionHtml: Six letters Q, Z, V, T, L and A are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figures below. Find the letter on the face opposite to Q.
questions.solution:
As V is common on both the dices, it is clear that Q, Z, T, and L are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. A will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

Z → L

Q → T

V → A

So, the opposite side of "Q" will be side "T".

questions.question: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.questionHtml: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution:
1) Total triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

As there are 3 same types of triangles, therefore total number of triangles will be (3 × 3) = 9 

2) As marked there are total 12 triangles.

Thus, there are total (9 + 12) = 21 triangles.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A - B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A $ B' means 'A is the son of B', 'A % B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A / B' means 'A is the wife of B' and 'A = B' means 'A is the brother of B'. Which of the following means A is the daughter of K? i. A + K / J - P = D ii. J % P = K + A = D iii. K + A / P - D % J iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B',
'A - B' means 'A is the father of B',
'A $ B' means 'A is the son of B',
'A % B' means 'A is the sister of B',
'A / B' means 'A is the wife of B' and
'A = B' means 'A is the brother of B'.

Which of the following means A is the daughter of K?
i. A + K / J - P = D
ii. J % P = K + A = D
iii. K + A / P - D % J
iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.solution:
iii. K + A / P - D % J → K is mother of A who is the wife of P who is the father of D who is the sister of J.

Here, A is the daughter of K.
